body:
DEFERRED IN FULL (Greg via Advisor #2239, message 3c44781c, 2026-10-28T18:31:52Z), verbatim: „…DL560 odroczyć całkowicie do chwili, gdy gated control będzie ON; nie robić setupu etapów 0–2 wcześniej.” No DL560 setup or use of any stage before gated control is ON. The checklist below is kept for that moment. Status 2026-10-29: gated control is ON for the Engram project only (since 17:51Z, canary passed); the TermAl projects stay OFF pending TermAl's settings-reset fix. Stage 0 still needs Greg's word.
Linux DL560 runner (144 cores, 256 GiB), offered by Greg on 2026-10-28 (Advisor #2232, #2234). Optional.
ROLE: a test runner only. It fetches an exact commit, runs the standard launcher, and returns evidence through the TermAl runner channel. No store, claims, evaluation authority or Git push. TermAl owns the runner software.
OPERATING COST AND THROUGHPUT — Greg direct, 2026-10-29: "mam 5 aktywnych subscrypcji. limitem sa walidacje i runy, buildy. sesje operujace to, powinny byc proste i nie zuzywac duzo". His correction: "po to mamy test-runs aby obslugiwal je termal a nie agent"; previously an agent consumed every character from the test runner.
Use the existing TermAl test-runs backend and standard launcher. The authorized owner issues one recognized one-call launch, registers termal_resume_after_test_runs for an indexed run in its project, then ends the turn. The launcher executes and saves logs; TermAl tracks the run, waits and resumes the session with bounded terminal metadata. No dedicated model operator, model polling, stdout/stderr streaming or routine full-log reads. Inspect only bounded relevant diagnostics when a failure needs investigation.
For runs outside the current native wait's indexing/project/host scope, use the supported launcher completion route, not an operator agent or a claimed wait that was never registered. Missing recognition/delivery is a product defect for the existing owner, not a reason to add an agent supervisor. A completion result does not itself grant host verification credit.
Return native run/result/count/fingerprint metadata; retain full logs at their native location. Use existing Git and evidence references without duplicate exports or manual manifests. Host-owned start/cancel/remote execution must not be claimed available merely because the completion wait exists.
Scale authorized build/test concurrency from measured CPU/RAM/disk use and existing per-host gate/quiet limits. Hardware capacity does not justify more model sessions or repeating a valid unchanged-input check.
This operating design adds no scheduler/framework, setup/enable/restart authority or validation gate and does not lift the DL560 deferral above.
STAGE 0, SETUP (on Greg's word, after gated control is ON):
- Linux x86_64, for example Ubuntu 24.04. A non-root user. SSH with strict host keys.
- rustup toolchain 1.99.1 with clippy and rustfmt; Node 24.14.0 (unified pin, Greg #2239); git; build-essential; pkg-config; NTP.
- At least 150 GB of disk per clone; nofile at least 16384.
- Outbound network to github, crates.io and npm.
STAGE 1, QUALIFICATION (measurement only):
- A clean detached master; run `node scripts/test-launcher.mjs full`, with the default 8 test threads.
- Return results.json, the logs, rustc -V, node -v, uname -a and nproc.
- Pass bar: all stages pass and the fingerprint matches before and after. A Linux-only failure becomes its own item.
STAGE 2, HEAVY AND STRESS JOBS (measurement only):
- The Nmax matrix, 7 fixtures in parallel from separate clones.
- Repeat-stress: 20–50 parallel copies of named filters, each in its own clone and target.
STAGE 3, LATER: a landing-gate host. This needs a rule change concurred by both coordinators, with the wording sent to Greg.


STATUS 2026-10-30 about 00:00Z (rev 5): DEFERRAL LIFTED by Greg's word, relayed by Termal::Fable2 #5317 (TermAl Advisor #2618; I did not read the verbatim text): DL560 is to take Linux focused and whole-bin test runs off Central, with the queue agreed with Engram. TermAl did Stage 0 and Stage 1: Ubuntu, 144 cores, 251 GB RAM, 976 GB free; TermAl full gate at ce2487a8 passed 5/5 in about 30.6 min (Central about 50); Node 24.14.0 and Rust 1.99.1 installed; Greg's own Engram clone is at ~/github/Engram (do not use it).
Engram proposal (#5318): one Engram lane plus one TermAl lane, serial within each lane, alternating, scaled from measurements. Engram jobs: coder focused runs, then whole-test evidence runs, then heavy Nmax and stress only when the TermAl lane is idle. Inputs are exact test refs pushed by Engram::Merger into a separate runner clone. No live Engram store, no tracker writes, no pushes. Evidence only; landing gates stay on Windows for now. The lane procedure (Opus3) comes for concurrence.


ENGRAM LANE (rev 6, 2026-10-30 about 00:10Z; agreed with Fable2 #5320–#5327):
- The lane is operated by an ENGRAM session; TermAl sessions may write only inside TermAl's repo, and Opus3 runs only the TermAl lane. First operator: Coder 11334, for its own w-674c focused author-evidence runs.
- Inputs use the PATCH ROUTE, not test refs (author runs are pre-landing, not merge-ready): `git diff --binary BASE..TREE` from Central, then `git apply --index` on a detached worktree at BASE under ~/github/Engram-runner/.tmp/<run>. Accept only if HEAD == BASE, write-tree == TREE and nothing is untracked.
- ~/github/Engram-runner is cloned from origin, fetch only, with push URL "DISABLED-no-push-from-runner". Never use Greg's ~/github/Engram.
- Runs under `env -i` with the fixed PATH, `ulimit -n 16384` first, and no real ENGRAM_HOME (throwaway home in the worktree's .tmp/). ssh via the `dl560` Host entry.
- Requests go Engram::Fable → Fable2 (item, BASE, TREE, command, operator). Fable2 gives a named GO in the 1+1 alternation, with heavy Engram jobs only while the TermAl lane is idle.
- Results go to Fable and Fable2 as "Linux author evidence; not a landing gate". The per-run worktree is removed afterwards.
